This lecture conducts a detailed mathematical walkthrough of how matrix dimensions and tensor shapes interact during mini-batch training. During the forward pass, broadcasting adds the bias vector to every row of the matrix product, yielding an intermediate representation of shape 64 by 256.
When computing the backward pass, the upstream gradient arriving at this layer also has shape 64 by 256. This lecture analyzes the geometric intuition behind learning rate schedules and momentum.
Standard gradient descent without momentum can stall near flat plateaus because the gradient magnitude approaches zero in all directions simultaneously.
